steps.say: ThreadPilot, the general manager’s co-pilot. One working day at a knitwear factory, on its own records: 1 April 2026.
07:00 · Before she asks, the day is on one screen: RED, 8 overdue, assembly below normal for 6 days, 3 decisions.
Each decision has one button. “Review options” runs the queue simulation for ORD-029, which will miss today.
Moving ORD-029 up saves it 5 days but adds 11 to six other orders, so it recommends keeping the current order.
Drafted before she asks: the two stalled orders already have a chase-up, written from the records.
“Review & send” opens the preview: to washing, 9 days idle, 3 days overdue. She reads it and confirms.
Sent and logged. Nothing went out before her click.
Every chart has an “i”. “Normal” means the previous 8 same weekdays, which cut false alerts from 0.67 to 0.1 a month.
The 07:00 briefing is written on a schedule: yesterday, what is at risk, what to decide.
